prerequisites: Basic and common subjects of the industrial branch from previous courses.

learning_outcomes.text: Possess the ability to design, develop, implement, manage and improve products, systems and processes in different industrial fields, using appropriate analytical, computational or experimental techniques.
Apply the acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them working in multidisciplinary teams.
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Possess the learning skills that allow continuous study throughout life for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into professional activities.
Know and apply the knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Organization and planning of projects and human teams. Teamwork and leadership capacity.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology and quality control.
Contribution from the professional practice of engineering to SDG 9: Build resilient infrastructure, promote sustainable industrialization and foster innovation.
Contribution from the professional practice of engineering to SDG 12: Ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology and quality control.
Applied knowledge of the main plastic deformation forming processes.
Applied knowledge of the main chip removal machining processes.
Applied knowledge of the operating fundamentals of manufacturing systems.
Applied knowledge of the main metal casting and molding processes.

syllabus_topics: Chip formation. Mechanics of orthogonal and oblique cutting. Cutting force
Non-conventional processes. High-speed machining. Electro-discharge machining (EDM)
Principles of metal and plastic molding
Machines and molds. Technical-economic design and process factors
Principles of metal forming by plastic deformation
Selection and integration of mechanical manufacturing processes
Manufacturing lines and assembly systems. Material handling
Operation of mechanical manufacturing systems. Productive factors: time, cost, quality and flexibility
Production environment: Elements of design, maintenance, productivity and sustainability of mechanical manufacturing systems
assessment_rules: Students have two opportunities to pass the course: an ordinary call and an extraordinary call. In the ordinary call, if the Progressive Evaluation Grade (CEP) is 5/10 or higher, the final grade is calculated as 0.55 * CEP + 0.45 * Global Exam Part 1 (EG1). If CEP is below 5/10 or the student chooses to take Global Exam Part 2 (EG2), the final grade is 0.55 * EG2 + 0.45 * EG1. To pass the course, a final grade of 5/10 or higher is required. The extraordinary call consists of a single written exam covering all course content, weighted 100%.
